name: Lesson 29 · I wonder if: indirect questions; als and wenn in the past

cards.front: I don't know **if** he's coming.
cards.back: Ich weiß nicht, **ob** er kommt.
cards.note: Indirect questions: ob and W-words, the verb at the end. ob turns a yes/no question into part of a sentence; its verb goes to the end.

cards.front: She's asking **whether** we have time.
cards.back: Sie fragt, **ob** wir Zeit haben.
cards.note: Indirect questions: ob and W-words, the verb at the end. ob: whether. Never wenn here: wenn is for conditions and times.

cards.front: Do you know if it **is going to rain** tomorrow? (one friend)
cards.back: Weißt du, ob es morgen **regnet**?
cards.note: Indirect questions: ob and W-words, the verb at the end. The verb of the ob clause goes last: regnet.

cards.front: I don't care **whether** it rains.
cards.back: Es ist mir egal, **ob** es regnet.
cards.note: Indirect questions: ob and W-words, the verb at the end. Es ist mir egal, ob…: I don't mind whether…. mir is the dative.

cards.front: I'm asking if you **can** help me. (one friend)
cards.back: Ich frage, ob du mir helfen **kannst**.
cards.note: Indirect questions: ob and W-words, the verb at the end. The modal goes last, after the infinitive.

cards.front: Ask him if he **is coming along**! (one friend)
cards.back: Frag ihn, ob er **mitkommt**!
cards.note: Indirect questions: ob and W-words, the verb at the end. At the end of the clause the separable verb is whole: mitkommt.

cards.front: Do you know if she **studies**? (one friend)
cards.back: Weißt du, ob sie **studiert**?
cards.note: Indirect questions: ob and W-words, the verb at the end. studieren: to study at university. Verbs in -ieren are regular.

cards.front: Can you tell me where the station **is**? (formal)
cards.back: Können Sie mir sagen, wo der Bahnhof **ist**?
cards.note: Indirect questions: ob and W-words, the verb at the end. The question word links the clauses, and the verb moves to the end. This is the polite way to ask.

cards.front: Do you know when the train **leaves**? (formal)
cards.back: Wissen Sie, wann der Zug **abfährt**?
cards.note: Indirect questions: ob and W-words, the verb at the end. At the end, abfahren is one word: abfährt.

cards.front: I don't know what that **costs**.
cards.back: Ich weiß nicht, was das **kostet**.
cards.note: Indirect questions: ob and W-words, the verb at the end. was … kostet: the verb last.

cards.front: Can you tell me what the ticket **costs**? (formal)
cards.back: Können Sie mir sagen, was die Fahrkarte **kostet**?
cards.note: Indirect questions: ob and W-words, the verb at the end. die Fahrkarte: the ticket for a bus or train.

cards.front: He's asking how old I **am**.
cards.back: Er fragt, wie alt ich **bin**.
cards.note: Indirect questions: ob and W-words, the verb at the end. wie alt … bin: the verb last.

cards.front: I have no idea where my key **is**.
cards.back: Ich habe keine Ahnung, wo mein Schlüssel **ist**.
cards.note: Indirect questions: ob and W-words, the verb at the end. keine Ahnung: no idea.

cards.front: Tell me why you **are laughing**! (one friend)
cards.back: Sag mir, warum du **lachst**!
cards.note: Indirect questions: ob and W-words, the verb at the end. warum … lachst: the verb last.

cards.front: Do you know who that **is**? (one friend)
cards.back: Weißt du, wer das **ist**?
cards.note: Indirect questions: ob and W-words, the verb at the end. wer … ist: the verb last.

cards.front: I'd like to know where you **live**. (formal)
cards.back: Ich möchte wissen, wo Sie **wohnen**.
cards.note: Indirect questions: ob and W-words, the verb at the end. wo Sie wohnen: the verb last.

cards.front: I don't know what he **wants**.
cards.back: Ich weiß nicht, was er **will**.
cards.note: Indirect questions: ob and W-words, the verb at the end. was er will: the verb last.

cards.front: **When** I was a child, I lived in a village.
cards.back: **Als** ich ein Kind war, habe ich in einem Dorf gewohnt.
cards.note: als and wenn in the past: once, or every time. als for one time or one stretch of time in the past. The verb goes to the end.

cards.front: **When** I was little, we had a dog.
cards.back: **Als** ich klein war, hatten wir einen Hund.
cards.note: als and wenn in the past: once, or every time. One period of the past: als. Then the main verb straight after the comma.

cards.front: **When** we were in Berlin, it was cold.
cards.back: **Als** wir in Berlin waren, war es kalt.
cards.note: als and wenn in the past: once, or every time. A single visit, so als.

cards.front: **When** he was a student, he had no money.
cards.back: **Als** er Student war, hatte er kein Geld.
cards.note: als and wenn in the past: once, or every time. als + war: one period of his life.

cards.front: **When** she had a fever, she stayed at home.
cards.back: **Als** sie Fieber hatte, ist sie zu Hause geblieben.
cards.note: als and wenn in the past: once, or every time. One occasion: als.

cards.front: **When** I was a pupil, I sometimes didn't feel like it.
cards.back: **Als** ich Schüler war, hatte ich manchmal keine Lust.
cards.note: als and wenn in the past: once, or every time. als for a time of life; manchmal: sometimes.

cards.front: **When** I was a student, I lived with my parents.
cards.back: **Als** ich Studentin war, habe ich bei meinen Eltern gewohnt.
cards.note: als and wenn in the past: once, or every time. als + one stretch of the past.

cards.front: **When** we arrived, it was late.
cards.back: **Als** wir angekommen sind, war es spät.
cards.note: als and wenn in the past: once, or every time. In a perfect at the end of the clause, the participle comes first and sind last.

cards.front: When were you in Italy? (one friend) – **When** I was twenty.
cards.back: Wann warst du in Italien? – **Als** ich zwanzig war.
cards.note: als and wenn in the past: once, or every time. wann asks the question; als answers it for the past.

cards.front: I went to university **when** I was nineteen.
cards.back: Ich bin zur Universität gegangen, **als** ich neunzehn war.
cards.note: als and wenn in the past: once, or every time. The als clause can also come second.

cards.front: **Whenever** I was at my grandparents', we always went for a walk.
cards.back: **Wenn** ich bei meinen Großeltern war, sind wir immer spazieren gegangen.
cards.note: als and wenn in the past: once, or every time. wenn in the past means whenever: something that happened again and again.

cards.front: **Whenever** we had holidays, we always went to Italy.
cards.back: **Wenn** wir Ferien hatten, sind wir immer nach Italien gefahren.
cards.note: als and wenn in the past: once, or every time. Every time, so wenn; immer makes the repetition clear.

cards.front: **Whenever** it was Christmas, we always ate cake.
cards.back: **Wenn** Weihnachten war, haben wir immer Kuchen gegessen.
cards.note: als and wenn in the past: once, or every time. Every Christmas, again and again: wenn.

cards.front: We often went for walks **when** the weather was nice.
cards.back: Wir sind oft spazieren gegangen, **wenn** das Wetter schön war.
cards.note: als and wenn in the past: once, or every time. oft: many times, so wenn, not als.
